question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `includeFamily` history contract plus a default-off `agents.defaults.experimental.sessionFamilyCarryover` flag that can prepend archived reset-family compaction summaries to embedded-agent prompts sent to the selected provider?
rationale: The code path is bounded and tested, but it adds protocol/config surface, persists reset lineage, and changes what archived context can reach the LLM boundary; automation cannot choose that product/security policy for maintainers.

options.title: Approve the explicit opt-in stack
options.body: Land after or with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90239, preserving default-off carryover and the documented `includeFamily` contract.

options.title: Split prompt carryover
options.body: Land only the family-history resolver/API path and defer automatic prompt carryover until archived-context-to-provider semantics have a separate approval path.

options.title: Reject core carryover
options.body: Keep reset-archive carryover out of core prompts and route future experimentation to a narrower plugin, tool, or explicit user-invoked history flow.

recommendation.title: Approve the explicit opt-in stack
recommendation.body: Land after or with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/90239, preserving default-off carryover and the documented `includeFamily` contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest current source and ownership signal across the affected session reset, gateway history, transcript, config, and repository policy surfaces.
